key_insight: fTNN replaces stochastic fractional-operator estimation with a fully deterministic, geometry-adapted tensor neural network that better handles boundary singularities in fractional PDEs.
engineering_relevance: The method offers a more accurate and scalable solver template for fractional Poisson and time-dependent fractional advection-diffusion problems in scientific computing.
method: Splits the fractional Laplacian into singular near-field, regular interior far-field, and analytical exterior far-field terms using a spatially varying near-field radius.
Uses Gauss-Jacobi, Gauss, and deterministic angular quadrature to evaluate the operator without Monte Carlo sampling.
Builds boundary-singularity-aware trial functions and a separable spatiotemporal network with alternating subspace optimization for time-dependent problems.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing high accuracy and substantial improvement over fPINN and Monte Carlo baselines, especially for strong boundary singularities and long-time simulations.
watch_item: Performance depends on correctly identifying singularity structure and selecting the leading boundary exponent, which may be difficult for complex geometries or unseen PDEs.
paper_title: fTNN: a tensor neural network for fractional PDEs
